facts.statement: Leinkupal laticauda was named and described in 2014 by Pablo Gallina, Sebastián Apesteguía, Alejandro Haluza, and Juan Canale.
facts.quote: In 2014, the type species Leinkupal laticauda was named and described by Pablo Gallina, Sebastián Apesteguía, Alejandro Haluza and Juan Canale.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MMCH-Pv 63-1 consists of a single front tail vertebra found in the Berriasian–Valanginian layers of the Bajada Colorado Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, MMCH-Pv 63-1, was found in a layer of the Bajada Colorado Formation dating from the Berriasian–Valanginian. It consists of a front tail vertebra.

facts.statement: The genus Leinkupal contains only one known species, Leinkupal laticauda.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Leinkupal laticauda.

facts.statement: Leinkupal fossils are known from the Early Cretaceous (Late Berriasian to Early Valanginian) of the Bajada Colorada Formation in the Neuquén Province of Argentina.
facts.quote: Leinkupal is a genus of diplodocine sauropod known from the Early Cretaceous (Late Berriasian to Early Valanginian stage) of the Bajada Colorada Formation, southeastern Neuquén Basin in the Neuquén Province of Argentina.

facts.statement: The front tail vertebrae of Leinkupal have extremely well-developed transverse processes that are as long as the vertebral body width and feature robust reinforcing ridges.
facts.quote: The front tail vertebrae have extremely well-developed transverse processes, as long as the width of the vertebral body, expanded sideways and to below, and possessing robust reinforcing ridges on their top and bottom surfaces.

facts.statement: Leinkupal is classified within the subfamily Diplodocinae of the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Leinkupal was placed in the Diplodocinae within the Diplodocidae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggests Leinkupal may be a sister species to the African genus Tornieria.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis indicated it was a possible sister species of Tornieria, discovered in Africa.

facts.statement: The deposits where Leinkupal was found represent a fluvial environment characterized by braided rivers.
facts.quote: These deposits represent a fluvial environment with braided rivers.

facts.statement: Leinkupal lived between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago during the Berriasian to Valanginian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (139.1 to 132.6 million years ago)
